# A field is more than a vector

[The same 96 physical values can occupy 96 or 288 storage slots. The distinction matters at every boundary.]{.lesson-deck}

[First six experiments · 2 of 6](../../start/index.qmd){.lesson-route-label}
:::

A `Field` connects a global domain, an owned index box, physical coordinates,
and storage.
Padding supports neighbouring-value calculations without changing which
physical values the rank owns.

## Geometry belongs to the field

For grid index $i$, physical position is $x=x_0+ih$. Our global x origin
is $-1$, spacing is $1/4$, and the owned box starts at global index four.
Its first x coordinate is therefore zero, even though its local index is zero.

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="storage" dedent=2}
```

Both fields receive $u(x,y,z)=1+x+y^2+z$ at every owned point.
`apply` supplies physical coordinates, including the owned box's global
offset. No separate coordinate array or rank-dependent correction is needed.

## Count values and count slots

The owned box has dimensions $4\times6\times4$, hence 96 values. A halo
width of one makes the padded extents $6\times8\times6$, hence 288 slots.
Its owned origin appears at storage offset

$$
1+6\cdot1+(6\cdot8)\cdot1=55.
$$ {#eq-padding}

`padded(0,0,0)` and `padded.data()[0]` therefore name different cells.
The former is an owned value; the latter is in the padding. The executable
compares all owned values between compact and padded representations and
prints the sizes and @eq-padding.

## Values can have components

Geometry and storage do not require scalar physics. For example:

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="components" dedent=2}
```

This is a field of three-component C++ values. It demonstrates container
generality; it does not imply that a scalar FFT or a scalar stepper accepts
the same component type without an adapter.

## Run, inspect, then change the padding

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --launcher=none
```

The empty JSON leaves these intentionally small constants in
[model.cpp](model.cpp). Predict the reported storage size and origin offset
for halo width two, then make that edit. The owned count and physical
initial condition should be unchanged. Update the independent expected
storage checks after doing the arithmetic yourself.

The program does not fill meaningful ghost values or calculate a stencil.
Padding allocates space; a halo exchange or boundary treatment supplies
its contents. The [heat lesson](../../heat/finite-differences/index.qmd)
shows that next step. The
[Field header](https://github.com/ahojukka5/OpenPFC/blob/master/include/openpfc/kernel/data/grid_field.hpp)
defines the ownership and indexing contracts.
The complete [C++ model](model.cpp) and [starting input](input.json)
are available with this lesson.
